vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: extract-memories
Version: 1.0.1

The 'extract-memories' skill is designed to summarize conversation highlights (decisions, preferences, and technical notes) and persist them in a local 'memory/' directory. It utilizes standard OpenClaw capabilities like FileWrite and sessions_spawn for background processing, and its instructions in SKILL.md are strictly aligned with its stated purpose without any evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or harmful prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill's claimed purpose (extracting and persisting conversation 'memories' into a memory/ directory) matches its instructions and requested permissions; nothing requested is disproportionate to that goal.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, workflow, and required permissions align: extracting the current conversation and appending summarized entries to memory/{{date}}.md reasonably requires FileWrite and may plausibly use a spawned background session for processing.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md limits actions to reading the current conversation context, extracting categorized short notes, writing them into memory/ files, and notifying the main session. It does not instruct reading unrelated files, environment variables, or external endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install steps or downloaded code — minimal surface area and nothing is written to disk by an installer.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables, credentials, or unrelated config paths are requested; FileWrite is the only explicit permission and matches the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill requests FileWrite and sessions_spawn (forking child agents). FileWrite is expected. sessions_spawn is plausible for background processing but increases capability scope (child agents can act autonomously); the skill does not request always:true and normal autonomous invocation is allowed by platform defaults.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill is coherent and low-risk in principle, but consider the following before installing:
- Verify where memory/ is stored (workspace path, host filesystem, cloud storage) and who/what can read it — sensitive data written there will persist.
- Confirm you are comfortable with automatic, end-of-conversation extraction; if not, prefer manual trigger (/extract-memories).
- Understand that sessions_spawn lets the agent fork background workers; if your environment restricts agent capabilities, review that policy.
- After enabling, inspect a few memory/{{date}}.md files to verify what is captured and remove or redact sensitive items; consider policies for retention and encryption.
- Because the skill is instruction-only, there is no installer risk, but you should still audit the produced files and storage location for privacy/security concerns.
